item.title: Missy Elliott Lands Icon Award With Janet Jackson Doing The Honors
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Missy Elliott landed a dance-community Icon Award, with longtime friend Janet Jackson set to present it at a cancer benefit.
item.content:encoded:
Missy Elliott earned another Icon Award, and the woman chosen to present it is someone she once mistook for a prank caller: Janet Jackson.

Missy was named this year’s Icon Award recipient at the Gala of the Stars. Jackson, who received the same award last year, will present it to Missy at the Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills on October 22.

The event raises money for Dancers Against Cancer, which helps dancers, choreographers and their families with the financial strain of cancer. The recognition puts Missy’s impact on dance alongside the music and videos that made her a Hip-Hop star.

“Missy Elliott represents everything the Icon Award celebrates. Her groundbreaking artistry has inspired generations of performers, and having Janet Jackson, last year’s honoree, present her with this award makes the moment even more special,” Noah Lands, the charity’s CEO and the gala’s executive producer, said in a statement.

The pairing has a personal history beyond awards shows. After Supa Dupa Fly arrived in 1997, Jackson was among the stars who reached out to Missy. The rapper later recalled that she didn’t believe the quiet voice on the phone was Jackson and hung up, thinking a friend was playing a joke.

Her manager then warned her that Jackson would be calling. “Oh my God, why didn’t you tell me? I just hung up on her!” Missy recalled in a 2022 Grammy.com interview.

That disbelief grew into a friendship that lasted well beyond their collaborations. In June 2022, Missy described how Jackson flew from London to spend two days with her after they talked about how much she missed seeing friends during the pandemic. They spent the visit laughing together, a break Missy said she had needed.

Dance has also remained central to how Missy brought her records to the stage. At the 2019 MTV Video Music Awards, she rebuilt several of her best-known video worlds for a medley. Alyson Stoner returned for “Work It,” reconnecting the performance with the dancer fans remembered from the original video. Jackson was among the artists who contributed tributes that night.

This year’s gala will also recognize Toni Basil with its Lifetime Achievement Award and Vincent Paterson with its Vanguard Award. Maksim Chmerkovskiy will host, with Chloé Arnold’s Syncopated Ladies among the performers.

The charity said last year’s gala raised $717,218. Its next fundraiser, with Jackson presenting Missy’s honor, takes place on October 22.

item.title: V.I The Boss Talks Pain Through “Hold Me Close” as Charting Accolades Add Up
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Chicago rapper V.I The Boss teams up with Feather on “Hold Me Close,” blending emotional storytelling, melodic R&B, and gritty rap.
item.content:encoded:
V.I The Boss is back with “Hold Me Close,” a new single featuring vocalist Feather that finds the Chicago rapper at his most exposed. It is a record that treats music less like a product and more like a means of getting through the night, and that approach separates it from nearly everything else dropping this week.

V.I The Boss has also added new chart milestones to his résumé, reaching No. 12 on the iTunes UK Hip-Hop/Rap chart. He also claimed No. 1 on both Amazon Music’s Hot New Releases chart in Rap and its overall Rap Best Sellers chart.

Sonically, the track takes its time. It starts hushed, like a secret being told after hours, and then keeps growing until R&B smoothness and Chicago rap toughness are sharing the same space. Feather supplies the melody; V.I supplies the truth. What comes out is a song that manages to be open-hearted without going soft, and sincere in a way that has become rare on release Fridays.

That sincerity is rooted in where he comes from. V.I The Boss spent his formative years in Chicago’s foster system, passed from one placement to another with no permanent address and no permanent people. Music was the one thing nobody could take from him, and it functioned as his coping mechanism years before it became his profession. Listeners can trace that origin story through every line he writes. His discography moves between turnt-up trap and the more introspective songs he calls pain music, and “Hold Me Close” lands right in the overlap, a record about craving stability from a partner when stability has always been a foreign concept.

Equally important is the résumé he built before going all-in on himself. For over ten years, V.I The Boss operated in the background of the business, helping other artists refine their sound, riding along on tours, and studying how deals and careers actually get made. The payoff is audible. “Hold Me Close” carries none of the frantic energy of a rookie trying to break through. It carries the confidence of somebody who already understands the game and his own place in it.

Pull Up Lam is behind the boards, laying down the dim, cinematic instrumental that holds the whole song together, and Delahoyne directed the official visual that dropped alongside it. As a package, the two feel like a formal introduction from an artist who has spent his entire life working up to this point.

Chicago’s rap history is full of names who made poetry out of pain, and V.I The Boss slots naturally into that lineage. But his version comes with something extra: a genuine warmth beneath the scars and a stubborn faith that reaching for other people is still worth the risk, even when experience says otherwise.

“Hold Me Close” featuring Feather is available now on every major platform. Stream it via Apple Music, watch the video on YouTube, and follow V.I The Boss on Instagram and X for future drops. Additional updates live on his official website, and his full catalog is one search away on any streaming app.

This is not a throwaway release. It is the moment V.I The Boss decided to let everyone in.

item.title: Star2 Drops New Concept Album 20-Something (In Love) ft. Young Henny Chinatown Runner, Ler Mu Dex, Lil BK & Seko
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Star2 returns with 20-Something (In Love), a deeply personal album exploring love, heartbreak, and resilience. Featuring Young Henny, Chinatown Runner, and more, the project follows the viral success of “M.O.B.” and “Never Again,” blending melodic trap with West Coast R&B.
item.content:encoded:
Following a massive 500K-video TikTok viral wave for “M.O.B.” and 1.2M YouTube views for “Never Again,” the San Diego-based Asian American hip hop trailblazer returns with his most personal and collaborative project yet

Asian American rapper and S2MG Records founder Star2 is back with his new album 20-Something (In Love). Anchored by the success of his viral hit “M.O.B.” and the melancholic visualizer for “Never Again,” which rocketed past 1.2 million views on YouTube, his new project is a definitive sonic statement on modern romance, vulnerability, and resilience.The album boasts an impressive lineup of genre-fluid collaborators, including long-time creative partner Young Henny, chinatown runner, Ler Mu Dex, Lil BK, and Seko. Together, this ensemble creates a rich sonic landscape that captures the chaotic emotional highs and lows of navigating love and ambitions in your twenties.“This album is for everyone trying to figure it out,” says Star2. “We brought together a family of artists to tell stories about late-night longing, heartbreak, and moving forward. It’s the most collaborative and honest work I’ve ever put out.”

Born in a Thai refugee camp before migrating to San Diego, Star2 has systematically built a loyal global following. 20-Something (In Love) marks a significant evolution in his artistry, seamlessly blending raw, melodic trap with West Coast R&B sensibilities.With a deep baseline catalog now featuring 5 albums, 4 EPs, and critical acclaim from hip hop tastemakers, Star2 continues to break boundaries for Asian American representation in mainstream music.

About Star2:

Star2 began his life in a Thai refugee camp where he was forced to flee genocide from the Burmese army in Myanmar who burned his village to the ground. A lottery in the camp brought him to San Diego with his grandmother and her four children, where he began a new life. Under the mentorship of esteemed producer Chico Bennett, his collaborations with acclaimed rappers include Soulja Boy, $tupid Young, Mozzy, MBNel, Luh Kel, Lil Poppa, HoodTrophy Bino, YSN Flow, and MarMar Oso to name a few. While not on tour, he documents his journey in the popular ‘Adventures of Star2’ series on YouTube. As an influential figure in Asian-American music, Star2 entwines heartfelt stories with captivating visuals, chronicling a tale of resilience and ascent. Esteemed platforms like Harper’s Bazaar Vietnam, GQ, HotNewHipHop, Ones to Watch, BET, and Lyrical Lemonade, among others, have celebrated his contributions.

Connect:

TIKTOK

YOUTUBE

INSTAGRAM

About Young Henny:

Young Henny was born Mookpolosoe in the Nu Po refugee camp on the Thai-Burma border. His Karen family had fled the Burmese military, hiding in the jungle until they reached the camp. In 2008, at nine years old, he landed in Akron, Ohio, in the middle of winter, seeing snow and a city for the first time. He grew up on the city’s North Side, where he taught himself English by watching PBS Kids before school and dealt with bullying and hate that hit close to home. A local church gave him a way forward. He picked up guitar and drums there and was leading worship by 14. After losing his father, he moved to Denver to chase music. There he met Star2, Ler Mu Dex and Chinatown Runner, and Star2 later flew him to San Diego to start work on the new album 20-Something (In Love). Now a husband and father living in Minnesota, Henny puts all of it into his music: the struggle, the faith, and the love that got him through. His message is simple. No matter how many times you hit rock bottom, pick yourself up and keep going.

item.title: Feds Accuse Ticket Broker Of Making $833K Off One Beyoncé Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Beyoncé’s Kansas City concert became a key example in a federal suit alleging a broker used 1,300 accounts to buy 7,624 tickets.
item.content:encoded:
Beyoncé’s Kansas City show allegedly netted a ticket broker more than $833,000 in resale profits after it used at least 1,300 accounts to buy seats, according to a new federal lawsuit.

The Justice Department sued REPS & Company and three executives on October 15, accusing them of getting around ticket-buying limits across thousands of events. The San Diego company allegedly bought 7,624 tickets to Beyoncé’s October 1, 2023, concert at Arrowhead Stadium, where the purchase limit ranged from four to eight.

That was the final stop on her “Renaissance World Tour.” The government put the broker’s profit from that one show at approximately $833,323.

DOJ trial attorneys Austin T. Mendes and Meredith L. Reiter laid out the alleged cost to fans in the complaint, which Mendes signed.

“Because Defendants mainly target and harvest tickets most likely to sell out and generate a high demand in the secondary marketplace, consumers that purchase the tickets Defendants resell often pay a significant markup,” the lawyers wrote.

The fight for seats had started months before Beyoncé reached Kansas City.

Ticketmaster’s original tour instructions required fans to register and undergo checks intended to screen out professional resellers. Demand could send fans into a lottery for an access code, and even getting a code did not guarantee a ticket.

Federal lawyers alleged that REPS took a different route. They described thousands of accounts, virtual credit cards and software that hid buyers’ locations. The complaint said most of its ticket-buying employees were based in the Philippines.

The company also allegedly kept an “Error Bible” to help staff overcome purchase blocks.

“The Error Bible instructs Defendants’ employees and agents on how to resolve or workaround Ticketmaster’s ticket limit controls, and they have developed and refined standard operating procedures for troubleshooting and bypassing ticket limits on Ticketmaster’s website,” Mendes and Reiter wrote.

Beyoncé’s concert was one example in a much larger case. The government alleged that REPS spent more than $1.3 billion to buy over 18.5 million tickets for at least 83,500 events in which it bought more than eight tickets.

The filing claimed that resales generated at least $120.8 million in profit.

The suit also named CEO Ryan Pancheri, President Brian Archibald and Chief Operating Officer Nicholas Totagrande. It accused them of violating the Better Online Ticket Sales Act, which bars bypassing online safeguards that enforce ticket limits and certain resales of tickets obtained that way.

REPS described its business on its website as using data to predict demand and prices, with a goal of connecting more fans to live events.

The company did not immediately respond to Billboard’s request for comment.

The government asked the Southern District of California court for a permanent order stopping the alleged conduct, financial relief and civil penalties. It did not specify a total dollar amount it wanted awarded.

item.title: Stones Throw Moves To Cut Los Retros Ties After Child Abuse Charges
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Stones Throw moved to end its Los Retros relationship after four felony charges, ahead of the label's anniversary festival.
item.content:encoded:
Stones Throw Records moved to break ties with Los Retros after the musician faced four child abuse-related felony charges, announcing its decision a day before the label’s 30th anniversary festival was due to begin.

The independent label addressed the case Thursday in a statement naming Mauri Tapia, who records as Los Retros. It said it had learned of the allegations the previous day and would keep reviewing the situation as more information emerged.

“In light of this information, we are taking steps to disassociate ourselves from Tapia and his work,” the label said.

Stones Throw did not explain what the separation would mean for its existing Los Retros releases.

The 26-year-old musician was charged October 12 in Ventura County Superior Court with four felony counts of unlawful acts with a child under 10, USA TODAY reported, citing court records. He had not entered a plea.

Los Retros was arrested October 8 and booked into jail the following day, with bail set at $3 million. The Ventura County Sheriff’s Office was investigating the case.

Stones Throw also clarified the timing of his canceled festival appearance. The label said it had announced that cancellation before learning about the allegations, separating the earlier booking decision from its latest move to distance itself from the musician.

The festival was set for October 16–18 in Los Angeles’ Highland Park neighborhood. Its lineup brought together artists from across Peanut Butter Wolf’s label history, including J. Rocc, Dâm-Funk, and the members of Lootpack. The current Friday listing no longer included Los Retros.

That relationship had extended beyond distributing records. In a 2019 Ones To Watch interview, Los Retros described working with Peanut Butter Wolf to help choose the six songs for his debut EP, Retrospect. The two considered several tracks before settling on the final release.

His music later became a commercial milestone for the company. In a 2024 interview, Peanut Butter Wolf identified Los Retros alongside Mild High Club as the artists behind Stones Throw’s first gold singles, placing the project among the label’s long-developing successes.

His next court appearance was scheduled for October 22.

item.title: A$AP Rocky Chases First Grammy With “Don’t Be Dumb”
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: A$AP Rocky revealed the Grammy goal behind *Don't Be Dumb* as his comeback album entered the first round of awards voting.
item.content:encoded:
A$AP Rocky revealed he made Don’t Be Dumb with a first Grammy win in mind, setting a clear goal for the album and ending his eight-year gap between projects.

The Harlem rapper discussed that push in a new Billboard interview as the first round of voting began.

“I think it would solidify everything that I worked hard for,” Rocky said. “I worked so hard on this, and I intentionally wanted to win one.”

He described a year in which music took the lead over his other work in fashion, film and directing. The album reached No. 1 after its January release. He also pointed to his arena shows as part of his case.

His submissions crossed genres. “Punk Rocky” went forward for Record of the Year, Best Music Video and Best Alternative Music Performance. The album also earned nominations for Album of the Year and Best Rap Album.

His Grammy record showed why a win would mark a new step. The Recording Academy listed three nominations and no wins. His first came in 2014 for Best Rap Song with “F***in’ Problems,” followed by Best Music Video nods for “L$D” in 2016 and “Tailor Swif” in 2025.

Two of those three chances came through his videos. “Punk Rocky” added to that body of work with a Winona Ryder-led visual. Rocky co-directed the clip with Folkert Verdoorn and Simon Becks, bringing his behind-the-camera work into the current awards push.

The latest campaign also extended beyond the screen. Rocky had added five December arena shows in Australia and New Zealand, with the promoter billing the run as his first return to the region in eight years.

The awards process still had several steps left. The first round opened on October 12 and was set to close on October 22. Eligible submissions went before voters to earn a place on the nominees list.

Music creators, including artists, songwriters, producers and engineers, cast the ballots. Final voting was scheduled for December 10 through January 7, ahead of the February 7, 2027 ceremony. The next test for Rocky’s Grammy bid was the nominations announcement on November 16.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Diddy Male Freak-Off Sex Worker Walks Back 12-Hour Confinement Claim
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Diddy accuser Clayton Howard acknowledged inaccuracies and sought to remove a 12-hour confinement claim before a key hearing.
item.content:encoded:
Clayton Howard acknowledged inaccuracies in his claims against Sean “Diddy” Combs and Cassie as he sought to remove an allegation that he was confined for approximately 12 hours.

He just asked permission to replace a proposed sixth amended complaint. Howard said he reviewed his account against his recollection and Diddy’s criminal trial record after reading the defense replies.

The dismissal motions target his fifth amended complaint.

“The revision corrects statements in Exhibit 1 that I concluded were inaccurate,” Howard wrote in a signed declaration.

The changes would remove the 12-hour claim from his account of a December 2016 Miami encounter, along with allegations that Diddy’s security personnel took his belongings.

Howard’s account included the length of that alleged confinement. His existing complaint, quoted in AllHipHop’s earlier coverage, described what he claimed happened after he was ordered away from the main suite.

“Plaintiff does not purport to describe events that occurred outside his presence, and, because of the music, did not hear what occurred in the master suite after he was ordered from it. Plaintiff’s agreement to attend the Miami encounter did not extend to being deprived of his clothing, identification, and telephone; to witnessing an assault; or to being confined for approximately twelve hours in a room he could not leave,” Howard wrote in that earlier complaint.

Howard also proposed dropping his California sexual-assault claim entirely and limiting his New York trafficking claim to Diddy.

The filing followed separate October 7 replies in which both defense teams pressed to end the suit without another amendment.

Cassie’s lawyer, Mélodie C. Han, argued that Howard had not linked the singer’s conduct to forced participation. Her team also argued that his account placed the alleged confinement after the sexual encounter, with Diddy controlling what happened.

“Based on Plaintiff’s own allegations, it was money that caused his participation, not coercion or fraud,” her team’s reply stated.

Diddy’s attorney Jonathan D. Gottlieb separately argued that Howard had not shown how alleged drugging or restraint caused a commercial sex act. His reply also challenged the attempt to hold Bad Boy Entertainment and CeOpco liable without specific facts about each company’s role.

Howard also sought to add details about staff arranging encounters. Representing himself, he said both defense teams opposed his new request.

item.title: Diddy & Dudus Fight Claim Shot Down By Federal Prison Officials
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Federal prison officials rejected the Diddy-Dudus fight claim while declining to explain the cause of his reported head injury.
item.content:encoded:
Federal prison officials flatly denied Diddy’s alleged fight with Christopher “Dudus” Coke on Thursday.

The Bureau of Prisons rejected the claim that the two men clashed at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey. A spokesperson told TMZ, “We can tell you that the story you are referring to is false and did not happen.”

Prison officials did not say what caused the reported injury. When asked how Diddy was hurt, the bureau declined to share more details.

The outlet stood by its account of a medical trip. It said Diddy left Fort Dix by ambulance early Saturday, October 10, for treatment of a head injury and returned before dawn. The report described the injury as non-life-threatening.

The agency’s denial followed the outlet’s report that Dudus fought with Diddy a day before that trip. That account linked the alleged clash to anger over raids and seized phones at the prison, citing sources inside Fort Dix.

Officials had given a more guarded response when news of the reported injury first broke.

Fort Dix told Us Weekly on October 12 that it would not discuss any prisoner’s housing or medical status. It cited privacy, safety and security.

Diddy’s team told the magazine it was still trying to confirm what happened. His representative said, “Sean’s health and well-being are our immediate concern.”

The official response came after sources close to Dudus had also denied the fight.

Nationwide Radio Jamaica said its newsroom spoke with those sources Wednesday evening. They said Dudus had never crossed paths with Diddy at Fort Dix. The station said their account led it to amend its first report.

Dudus’ aunt, Angela Jackson, had also rejected the claim. Nationwide cited her Instagram statement saying the men had never met and were held in different sections of the prison. The broadcaster did not name the separate sources it interviewed.

Diddy was serving a 50-month term after his federal trial. Jurors convicted him of two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution and acquitted him of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking.

His legal team appealed his conviction and sentence. In an October 7 statement to Us Weekly, his spokesperson said, “Sean remains focused on serving his time.”

item.title: Adrien Broner & DeenTheGreat Turn Kai Cenat Feud Into Diss Track
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Adrien Broner and DeenTheGreat targeted Kai Cenat in “Purple App Killa,” while Lemuel Plummer offered a different view of the feud.
item.content:encoded:
Former four-division boxing champion Adrien Broner and DeenTheGreat took their feud with Kai Cenat into the studio and released “Purple App Killa,” a new diss track and music video with Hitmaka.

DeenTheGreat named Kai Cenat as the target when he announced the October 15 release. “KAI CENAT DISS TRACK OUT NOW,” he wrote in a post on X, directing fans to the full video.

The pair had already shared behind-the-scenes footage of work on the song and its music video before the finished clip went live. Broner and DeenTheGreat both appeared as collaborators on the official upload, which ran just under three minutes.

The release followed DeenTheGreat’s public complaint about visiting Kai’s Vivet clothing stand at ComplexCon. He said he came to support the brand and spend money but felt like a random fan.

Their complaints circulated on October 5, more than a week before DeenTheGreat announced the finished track.

He and Ray J discussed the dispute with Zeus Network founder Lemuel Plummer, who had a different account of his own visit to the stand.

NDTV Sports reported that Plummer bought six outfits from Vivet. During the exchange, DeenTheGreat argued that Kai should have given Plummer clothes for free.

Plummer said he had chosen to pay because he wanted to support the business. He also said Kai had thanked him for coming through.

“I bought it. I wanted to support it,” Plummer said.

DeenTheGreat kept pressing the point about the clothes. Plummer instead credited Kai with building the brand with his own money and described a warm reception at the booth.

He offered to call Kai during the discussion. DeenTheGreat told him not to bother. Plummer held to his own account: “Well, he did give me respect.”

As the diss video arrived, DeenTheGreat also had a live event with Hitmaka and KICK. The platform billed the producer as the DJ for its COB Halloween Bash, a Miami party presented by KICK and DeenTheGreat.

The event was billed as KICK-exclusive. DeenTheGreat posted that the bash was live shortly after he announced the song.

item.title: Marsha Blackburn’s Kendrick Lamar AI Ad Triggers ELVIS Act Warning
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Marsha Blackburn called her Kendrick Lamar AI clip a “funsie” as a Nashville attorney questioned whether its use had clearance.
item.content:encoded:
Marsha Blackburn’s AI take on Kendrick Lamar’s Super Bowl show drew a legal warning from a Nashville attorney, who said the campaign post could run afoul of Tennessee’s ELVIS Act if the rapper hadn’t approved its use.

Entertainment lawyer Kaley Bonett told WKRN that she viewed the clip as a campaign ad. She pointed to Kendrick Lamar’s voice and his halftime choreography to explain why clearance mattered.

Bonett is an associate at Hall Booth Smith, where she works on entertainment and intellectual property matters.

Blackburn said a county commissioner made the video, and she and other Republicans reposted it.

“We re-posted it, and it’s a funsie. Everybody got out and vote,” she said.

The senator posted the clip October 13 to promote early voting in her run for Tennessee governor. It cast her in Kendrick Lamar’s Super Bowl role, with AI versions of other Tennessee Republicans joining the performance. Democratic rival Jerri Green criticized the post.

The earlier backlash also highlighted Blackburn’s push to protect artists from AI copies of their voices and faces.

On September 30, Blackburn asked the Senate to pass the NO FAKES Act without objection. She argued that artists, songwriters and other Americans needed protection from harmful deepfakes made without their consent.

The bill would create federal rights over AI replicas of a person’s voice and face, with a process to seek their removal from online platforms. Sen. Ted Cruz blocked that attempt, saying the measure needed stronger free-speech protections.

Blackburn pushed back. She said the bill already included language to protect political commentary, criticism, satire and parody. That exchange showed how permission and free speech had become central to her own case for federal action.

Tennessee’s ELVIS Act took effect July 1, 2024. It added voice protections to state law, covering both real and simulated voices that people can identify. It allows claims for certain uses made without consent and lets courts order them to stop.

The state law also allows news, public affairs, criticism, satire and parody when the First Amendment protects those uses. Those speech protections sit alongside the voice rights Bonett raised in her assessment.

Before its October 15 update, the station reported no response to its requests for further comment from Blackburn or Kendrick Lamar’s team.
